hud.days_strip: The 30 days of the mission; dark ones are the lunar night
hud.night_now: Lunar night: {dias} days without sun left
module.recycler.what: Cleans the air and recycles water.
module.greenhouse.what: Grows food. Uses a little water.
module.workshop.what: Repairs modules and sends the rover. It also powers the antenna: with it, Earth warns you about storms.
tablet.budget.left: {quedan} of {total} left to share. What you do not use is stored in the battery.
tablet.budget.none: You shared out all the energy.
coach.welcome.title: You are the commander of this base
coach.welcome.crew: You look after {personas} astronauts on the Moon.
coach.welcome.energy: Your job: share the energy from the Sun.
coach.welcome.night: On day {noche} the lunar night arrives: {duracion} days with no Sun. Save battery before it.
coach.welcome.lose: If air or food reach 0, the mission is cancelled and everyone returns to Earth.
coach.pick_recycler: Tap the Recycler. It gives us air and water.
coach.power_recycler: Press + until you reach {reciclador}. Watch the air go up right above.
coach.pick_greenhouse: Nice! Now tap the Greenhouse: that is where food grows.
coach.power_greenhouse: Fill the Greenhouse to {invernadero} or more. Without it, food drops {comida} every day.
coach.verdict: This stamp shows how the base will be tomorrow. What you do not share is saved in the battery.
coach.execute: Check the stamp: it shows how the base will end up. Press "Play the day".
coach.night: Night arrives in {faltan} days. Save battery!
help.title: How to play
help.goal: Your mission: get the {personas} people on the base safely to day {dias}.
help.step1: Tap a module and decide how much energy to give it.
help.step2: Check the notice: it tells you how the base will be tomorrow.
help.step3: Press "Play the day". What you do not spend is saved in the battery.
help.life_support: Air and water. Drops {aire} every day. The Recycler raises it. At 0 the mission is cancelled.
help.food: Drops {comida} every day. The Greenhouse raises it. At 0 the mission is cancelled.
help.battery: Stored energy. At night it is all you have.
help.dose: Radiation is invisible energy from the Sun that harms the body. It is measured in mSv. If it fills the circle, the mission is cancelled.
help.night: From day {noche} on, {duracion} days with no Sun. Arrive with a full battery.
help.workshop: Repairs modules, sends the rover and powers the antenna that warns of storms. Only works with {taller} or more.
help.storm: In a solar storm you choose: shelter (almost no radiation, but less production) or keep working (more radiation).
event.storm.title: Solar storm incoming!
event.storm.text: The Sun launched a {tipo}{detalle}: a cloud of particles that harms the body. It arrives in a few hours. What do we do?
event.breakdown.title: Breakdown: {modulo}
event.breakdown.text: A part of {modulo} broke. It will produce nothing until you repair it.
event.ice.title: Ice detected
event.ice.text: We found ice in a nearby crater. Ice is water: for drinking and for making air.
event.night_warning.title: The lunar night is coming
event.night_warning.text: Soon the Sun will hide behind the crater. No Sun means no new energy. Charge the battery now!
event.effect.rover_gain_maybe: Tomorrow (or the day after): +{valor} life support
debrief.abort: The crew returned safely to Earth in the emergency ship.
debrief.win.stars1: You made it, but something was very tight. Save more battery before the night.
debrief.win.stars2: Good job! You saved energy for the night and nobody was in serious danger.
debrief.win.stars3: Perfect mission! You always had energy to spare. That is how a real commander plans.
debrief.cause.life_support: Air and water ran out. The Recycler needed more energy.
debrief.cause.food: Food ran out. The Greenhouse needs energy almost every day.
debrief.cause.radiation: The crew got too much radiation. The shelter and the Shielding keep it low.
debrief.night_long: The night lasted longer than your battery. Without the Sun, you can only use what you saved before.
debrief.decisive.life_support: It all started on day {dia}, when air and water dropped below 25.
debrief.decisive.food: It all started on day {dia}, when food dropped below 25.
debrief.decisive.radiation: It all started on day {dia}, when radiation passed 70% of the limit.
debrief.rewind: Go back to day {dia} and try again
debrief.chart.title: Your mission, day by day
debrief.chart.aria: Chart of life support, food, battery and radiation during the mission. Use the button below to see the data as a table.
debrief.share.win: I kept a base running for {dias} days at the Moon's south pole with {estrellas} in Shackleton: Night Shift.
debrief.share.loss: I reached day {dia} running a base at the Moon's south pole in Shackleton: Night Shift. Next time I make it to 30!
menu.pitch: You are in charge of {personas} astronauts for {dias} days on a science expedition.
menu.mission.cadete.what: Your first mission. With room to learn.
menu.mission.comandante.what: The full challenge. Every decision counts.
crew.title: Meet your crew
crew.valeria.name: Valeria Andrade
crew.valeria.quote: Every drop of water is recycled. If the Recycler stops, we all feel it when we breathe.
crew.mateo.name: Mateo Quishpe
crew.mateo.quote: If the greenhouse runs out of light, I run out of lettuce.
crew.amaru.name: Amaru Tene
crew.amaru.quote: When the Sun gets angry, we go to the shelter. No arguing.
crew.lucia.name: Lucía Herrera
crew.lucia.quote: Give me ten energy in the workshop and I will fix anything. Even the rover.
title.subtitle: NIGHT SHIFT
title.pitch: You are in charge of 4 astronauts for thirty days at the Moon’s south pole.
title.team: Team Halo Sur · NASA Space Apps 2026 · Sangolquí, Ecuador
crew.hint: Tap an astronaut to meet them.
sun.compact: Sun active today: {tipo} on {fecha} (level {nivel}) · NASA DONKI
crew.valeria.good: The air is clean and the water flows. Good job, {nombre}!
crew.valeria.worried: {nombre}, air and water are dropping. The Recycler needs more energy.
crew.mateo.good: The lettuce is growing happily, {nombre}! Salad for everyone.
crew.mateo.worried: {nombre}, the pantry is emptying. The Greenhouse needs energy.
crew.amaru.good: Radiation is under control, {nombre}. I keep watching the Sun.
crew.amaru.worried: {nombre}, we have taken a lot of radiation. More Shielding, please.
crew.lucia.good: Everything works, {nombre}. My tools can rest.
crew.lucia.worried: {nombre}, something is failing or the battery is very low. I am on it.
debrief.voice.life_support: We ran out of air and water, {nombre}!
debrief.voice.win: We did it, {nombre}! Thirty days on the Moon.
debrief.tip.life_support: give the Recycler more energy every day, and save battery before the night.
debrief.tip.food: don't leave the Greenhouse without energy: plants need it almost every day.
debrief.tip.radiation: during storms, everyone to the shelter; and power the Shielding.
warn.title: Message from Earth: solar storm in {dias} days
warn.title_one: Message from Earth: solar storm tomorrow
warn.advice: Charge the battery and get the Shield ready.
help.antenna: The Workshop also powers the antenna. With it, Earth warns you about storms {aviso} days ahead. A signal takes just over 1 second to reach the Moon; to Mars, between 4 and 24 minutes!
sources.button: Where does the data come from?
sources.title: Where does the data come from?
sources.intro: This game mixes real NASA data with made-up parts so it is playable. Here is which is which.
sources.error: We could not load the list right now. Please try again in a bit.
science.title: Real science
science.iss: On the Space Station, a NASA instrument measured about {dosis} micrograys of radiation per day (April 2022 average).
science.iss_hint: The gray is the unit that measures the radiation a body absorbs.
coach.welcome.goal: Last {dias} days and we all go home.
coach.greenhouse: Now the Greenhouse: give it {invernadero}. Watch the food go up above.
loading.tip.1: Save battery before the lunar night arrives.
loading.tip.2: If a solar storm is coming, send the crew to the shelter.
loading.tip.3: Tap a module of the base to give it energy.
loading.tip.4: Energy you don’t hand out is stored in the battery.
loading.tip.5: The Recycler makes air and water. The Greenhouse makes food.
loading.tip.6: If something goes wrong, the report lets you go back to an earlier day.
onb.1.title: Your mission
onb.1.a: You are in charge of {personas} astronauts for {dias} days at the Moon’s south pole.
onb.1.b: Keep them safe until the relief ship arrives.
onb.2.title: Energy
onb.2.a: The Sun charges your battery. Each day you share that energy among the modules.
onb.2.b: Energy you don't use is saved in the battery, until it is full.
onb.3.title: Today's plan
onb.3.a: Each day you choose how much energy each module gets, then press "Pass the day".
onb.3.b: You can tap the modules on the base or use the panel.
onb.4.title: What is coming
onb.4.night.name: Lunar night
onb.4.night.text: Several days without Sun. Fill your battery first.
onb.4.storm.name: Solar storms
onb.4.storm.text: Dangerous particles. Decide if you go to the shelter.
onb.4.repair.name: Breakdowns
onb.4.repair.text: Something breaks. Fix it with the Workshop.
onb.4.ice.name: Ice
onb.5.title: How you win and lose
onb.5.win: You win: you reach day {dias} with the whole crew safe.
onb.5.lose: You lose if air and water run out, food runs out, or radiation passes the limit.
onb.5.safe: If you lose, the crew returns safely in the emergency ship.
onb.6.title: Your crew
onb.6.a: Each one looks after a module. Their faces tell you how things are going.
coach.hint_day2: Here you see today's energy: Sun, battery and what you can share.
coach.hint_day3: This stamp tells you how the base will be tomorrow.
eflow.tip.sun: Energy the panels make today from sunlight.
eflow.tip.no_sun: It is night: the panels make no energy. You only have your battery.
eflow.tip.battery: It saves the energy you do not use. If it fills up, the extra is lost.
eflow.tip.spend: Sun + battery − {base} the base uses. This is what you share today. These are game energy units.
eflow.base: The base uses {base} just by being switched on.
board.after_today: Air & water {aire} · Food {comida} · Battery will be {bateria}
sunfc.title: Sun forecast: next days
repair.title: {modulo} is broken
repair.need: You need {min} free energy to repair.
repair.in_progress: Ready when the day ends. Lucía is on her way.
info.storm.1: The Sun threw out very fast particles.
info.storm.2: On Earth, the atmosphere protects us.
info.storm.3: On the Moon, nothing slows them down.
info.storm.alt: Drawing: the Sun sends particles (level {nivel} of 4) toward the lunar base. On Earth a shield bends them away; on the Moon nothing stops them.
info.night.1: At the south pole the Sun always hangs very low.
info.night.2: When it slips behind the mountains, your base sits in shadow for days.
info.night.alt: Drawing: the Sun sinks and hides behind the mountains; the base falls into shadow.
info.breakdown.2: Fixing it costs {min} energy from the Workshop.
info.breakdown.alt: Drawing: the broken part of {modulo} throws sparks. Fixing it costs {min} energy from the Workshop.
info.ice.1: Some craters never get any light.
info.ice.2: There, water stayed frozen for millions of years.
info.ice.alt: Drawing: a crater in permanent shadow with ice at the bottom and the rover on the rim.
info.dust.1: Moon dust is fine and sticks to everything.
info.dust.2: It covers the panels, so they give less energy.
info.dust.alt: Drawing: dust stuck on a solar panel blocks the light; a rover cleans it with a brush.
crew.panel.title: Your crew
log.act.missed: Act {act} is over. Goal not reached, but the mission goes on.
log.dust: Moon dust on the solar panels: they make less power.
log.dust.clean: Decision: clean the panels with the rover.
log.dust.tilt: Decision: tilt the panels. The dust stays until it is cleaned.
log.dust.cleaned: Panels clean: they make full power again.
log.dust.failed: The panels could not be cleaned: the Workshop had no energy.
log.harvest: Extra harvest in the greenhouse: +{amount} food.

act.2.name: The Sun wakes up

act.3.pill: Night without running out of energy

act.4.goal: Recover everything: above half by day {dia}.

act.pill_aria: Act {n} goal: {meta}. Tap to read it again.
act.state.go: You have not reached the goal yet.
act.state.lost: This goal was lost. Keep going.
act.missed: Almost. See what happened and try another idea.
unlock.workshop: Workshop and rover ready! You can now repair and explore.
unlock.shield: Shield and Shelter active! They protect you from the storm.
unlock.generic: {module} is ready! You can use it now.
lock.title: Under construction
ff.stopped.event: I stopped: something happened. Take a look.
ff.stopped.low: I stopped: a resource is low. You decide.
ff.stopped.night_soon: I stopped: night is coming. Get ready.
ff.stopped.act: I stopped: a new act begins.
ff.stopped.invalid_plan: I stopped: your plan no longer fits. Change it.
event.dust.title: Dust on the panels
dust.title: Dusty panels: they give less energy
dust.on: Cleaning in progress: ready at the end of the day
dust.need: You need {min} free energy in the Workshop.
eflow.tip.dust: Dust covers the panels: they give {pct}% less.
event.harvest.title: Extra harvest
event.harvest.text: The greenhouse gave more food than expected.
coach.d2_flow: Up top: radiation, the day and energy. What is left over is saved.
coach.d2_pass: Share power with + and −. Above each bar you see how it changes.
coach.d3_harvest: Extra harvest! The greenhouse gave more food. Press "Great!".
coach.d3_forecast: The stamp shows how the base will end up. Check it before you play the day.
coach.d3_pass: Adjust the power if you like. Then play the day.
coach.d4_dust: Dust! There are TWO options. Each gains and loses something. Pick yours.
coach.d4_workshop: The Workshop opened. It repairs modules and sends the rover.

coach.d5_goal: This is the goal of the act: air and food above {meta}. Last day!
coach.d5_pass: Play day 5 to finish the tutorial.
coach.low_air: Air is low! Give the Recycler more energy.
coach.low_food: Food is low! Give the Greenhouse more energy.
onb.t.win: You win the act if air and food stay above {meta} on day 5.
onb.t.lose: In the real mission, you lose if air or food runs out.
onb.t.safe: Here you practice: you cannot lose.
tut.done.title: Tutorial complete!
tut.done.sub: You know the basics of the base.
tut.done.l2: You look after air and food.
tut.done.l3: You decide when an event arrives.
menu.mission.tutorial.what: Learn to play. 5 guided days, no losing.
comic.label: Fictional story · real data
comic.1.title: Year 2048
comic.1.b: A ship is flying to the Moon.
comic.1.c: It will build the first home away from Earth.
comic.2.title: Shackleton crater
comic.2.a: It sits at the Moon’s south pole.
comic.2.b: The Sun almost always shines on its rim. That is where power comes from.
comic.2.c: Deep in the dark bottom sleeps very old ice.
comic.3.title: One base, four people
comic.3.a: Valeria, Mateo, Amaru and Lucía arrive at the base.
comic.3.b: Each one knows how to do something important.
comic.3.c: Together they take care of their little home.
comic.4.title: Solar storm
comic.4.a: The Sun throws a huge storm.
comic.4.b: Direct contact with Earth is cut off.
comic.4.c: Only short alerts reach the antenna.
comic.5.title: You have 30 days
comic.5.a: You decide how to share the power.
comic.5.b: Protect the crew from radiation and get through the lunar night.
comic.5.c: Hold on until the relief ship arrives.
log.challenge.failed: Challenge {challenge} did not work out. We learn and go on.
log.challenge.skipped: You skipped challenge {challenge}. There will be another day.
ff.stopped.challenge: I stopped: there is a challenge today. Give it a try!
challenge.assist.off: Tip: put power in {place} before the challenge for an edge.
challenge.effect.no_warnings: No warnings from Earth until day {day}
challenge.result.perfect: Great work, commander! The base notices.
challenge.result.partial: Close. Something went well, something did not.
challenge.result.failed: Not this time. It happens on real missions too.
challenge.day02_rover_ice.title: Rover to the ice
challenge.day02_rover_ice.text: There is ice in the crater. Drive the rover there and come back.
challenge.day02_rover_ice.how: Tap an arrow to move the rover. Bring the ice to the base.
challenge.day02_rover_ice.science: Near the Moon's south pole, some craters stay in shadow forever. They may hold water ice.
challenge.day02_rover_ice.learn: Sun gives energy but brings radiation. Shade protects but drains battery.
challenge.rover.hint: In the Sun you charge, but radiation goes up.
challenge.rover.got_ice: You have the ice! Now go back to the base.
challenge.rover.on_sun: Sun: recharges battery, but radiation rises.
challenge.rover.on_shade: Shade: no radiation, but it drains battery.
challenge.rover.end.home: Back at base with the ice!
challenge.rover.end.battery: The rover ran out of battery.
challenge.rover.end.dose: Too much radiation. The rover stops.
challenge.day04_solar_radar.title: Space weather antennas
challenge.day04_solar_radar.text: The antennas must catch the Sun's signal. Match their waves.
challenge.day04_solar_radar.how: Move each slider until your wave covers the reference.
challenge.day04_solar_radar.science: NASA watches solar storms and warns when one heads toward Earth.
challenge.day04_solar_radar.learn: With good antennas, Earth warns you before storms.
challenge.day06_hull_seals.title: Leaks in the tunnels
challenge.day06_hull_seals.text: Three leaks are hiding in the corridors. Find them and seal them.
challenge.day06_hull_seals.how: Tap a zone to scan it. The detector says if a leak is near.
challenge.day06_hull_seals.science: Space bases need well-sealed walls. That keeps the air from escaping.
challenge.day06_hull_seals.learn: Scanning smartly saves tries. Use the clues.
challenge.day08_comm_cables.title: Cables to the beacons
challenge.day08_comm_cables.text: The beacons need three cables. Connect them without crossing.
challenge.day08_comm_cables.how: Drag from each letter to its match. Cables cannot cross.
challenge.day08_comm_cables.science: Cables carry data, power and measurements. Each one needs its own path.
challenge.day08_comm_cables.learn: Planning the path first saves time.
challenge.cab.hint: Press a letter and slide across the squares to its match.
challenge.cab.msg.far: Tap a square right next to the cable end.
challenge.day12_robotic_arm.title: Robotic arm
challenge.day12_robotic_arm.text: It is night. The arm must pick up a shiny sample.
challenge.day12_robotic_arm.how: Turn with buttons 1 and 2, or drag the arm. Then press Grab.
challenge.day12_robotic_arm.science: Robotic arms collect soil samples without anyone going out onto the surface.
challenge.day12_robotic_arm.learn: Going slowly and watching the distance helps you avoid crashes.
challenge.day12_robotic_arm.assist: You get more battery and one extra try.
challenge.arm.alt: Robotic arm with two joints, a sample and rocks
challenge.arm.hint: Bring the tip to the sample without touching rocks.
challenge.arm.msg.miss: Not yet. Bring the tip closer.
challenge.arm.msg.blocked: The arm touches a rock. Find another way.
challenge.day14_biomed_check.title: Crew check-up
challenge.day14_biomed_check.text: Today we check on the crew. Help whoever needs it most.
challenge.day14_biomed_check.how: See who is unwell. Drag a care card onto that person.
challenge.day14_biomed_check.science: On real missions, astronaut health is watched closely.
challenge.day14_biomed_check.learn: Reading the signs helps you care for each person.
challenge.bio.pending: Pick someone and a care for each card.
challenge.day18_micrometeorites.title: Micrometeorite shower
challenge.day18_micrometeorites.text: Tiny rock grains fly very fast toward the base. Protect the panel.
challenge.day18_micrometeorites.how: Turn the shield to where the radar warns.
challenge.day18_micrometeorites.science: Spacecraft use Whipple shields: thin, spaced layers. They break up a grain before it gets through.
challenge.day18_micrometeorites.learn: Several thin layers stop a grain better than one thick layer.
challenge.day18_micrometeorites.assist: The shield is wider and you get more warning.
challenge.day24_super_storm.title: Great solar storm
challenge.day24_super_storm.text: A big made-up storm arrives. It is like the real ones NASA measures.
challenge.day24_super_storm.how: Pick what to switch off. Then place the wall where the bursts come from.
challenge.day24_super_storm.play: Move the wall to where the radar warns.
challenge.day24_super_storm.science: Water and moon dust slow down particles from the Sun. Shelters use them for that.
challenge.day24_super_storm.learn: Saving power in time helps protect the crew.
challenge.day24_super_storm.assist: The wall is wider and you get more warning.
challenge.day24_super_storm.choice.q: What do you do with the battery?
challenge.day24_super_storm.choice.off.t: A wider wall, but no harvest today.
challenge.day24_super_storm.choice.on.te: A normal wall, and the Greenhouse keeps going.
challenge.sector.radar_alt: Radar with {n} sectors around the base
challenge.day16_regolith_trench.title: Regolith wall
challenge.day16_regolith_trench.text: Cover the module with regolith. Then radiation arrives weaker.
challenge.day16_regolith_trench.how: Collect the piles and dodge the rocks. Each pile is a brick for the wall.
challenge.day16_regolith_trench.science: Regolith is the dust and loose rock of the Moon. A thick layer helps slow down radiation.
challenge.day16_regolith_trench.learn: Each pile adds to the wall. More regolith protects the module better.
challenge.trench.hint: Tap an arrow to move forward.
challenge.trench.bump: You hit a rock! You use one repair.
challenge.trench.got: One more brick for the wall!
challenge.trench.end.done: You made it! The wall protects the module.
challenge.trench.end.broken: The robot needs a rest. It keeps what it collected.
challenge.day30_relay_docking.title: The relief ship arrives
challenge.day30_relay_docking.text: It is the last day. The relief ship reaches the base. Help it dock.
challenge.day30_relay_docking.how: Press Lock when the mark is inside the zone.
challenge.day30_relay_docking.science: A ship docks with a station very carefully. It moves slowly and lines up bit by bit.
challenge.day30_relay_docking.learn: Each crew member adjusts one part. Working together, docking goes better.
challenge.relay.how_reduced: Move each cursor up or down into the zone and press Lock.
challenge.relay.end.some: The ship arrived! It docked a little crooked.
challenge.relay.end.few: The ship arrived safe! It docked slowly.

challenge.demo.seals.s2: The alert says if a leak is near

challenge.demo.relay.s2: Press the lock inside the zone
practice.title: Mission minigames
practice.text: Try each challenge as many times as you like. Nothing is won or lost here.
challenge.bio.pick_care: Drag a care card to whoever needs it. {n} left.
challenge.bio.ready: Ready. Press Confirm, or tap a card to take it back.
